Why this is correct:
Labuan FSA develops and regulates Labuan IBFC.

Why the other options are wrong:
A — This assigns the role to the wrong regulator or authority.
B — This assigns the role to the wrong regulator or authority.
C — This assigns the role to the wrong regulator or authority.

Exam cue: Match the regulator to its lane: BNM = financial institutions, monetary policy, money/FX and payments; SC = capital markets and licensed persons; Bursa = exchange infrastructure; PIDM = protection schemes; Labuan FSA = Labuan IBFC.
What happens to an existing bond’s price when the required yield rises?
Yield has no effect on price.
When required yield rises, a fixed-rate bond price falls.

Answer: D — When required yield rises, a fixed-rate bond price falls.

Why this is correct:
Bond price and required yield move inversely.

Why the other options are wrong:
A — “Yield has no effect on price” is not the best answer because the question is testing the inverse bond price-yield relationship, and this option changes or misapplies that rule.
B — “Price always equals par” is not the best answer because the question is testing the inverse bond price-yield relationship, and this option changes or misapplies that rule.
C — “When yield rises, price rises” is not the best answer because the question is testing the inverse bond price-yield relationship, and this option changes or misapplies that rule.

Exam cue: Bond MCQs often test the inverse price-yield rule, YTM vs coupon/par-discount-premium, duration as interest-rate sensitivity, credit ratings as default-risk assessments and callable-bond reinvestment risk.
Which answer best applies the study text requirement on fit and proper requirements?
An undischarged bankrupt or person convicted of fraud would fail minimum fit and proper criteria.

Answer: D — An undischarged bankrupt or person convicted of fraud would fail minimum fit and proper criteria.

Why this is correct:
Minimum criteria include not being bankrupt, not being a judgment debtor and no fraud/dishonesty/violence conviction.

Why the other options are wrong:
A — This fails one of the fit-and-proper, examination or CPE requirements.
B — This fails one of the fit-and-proper, examination or CPE requirements.
C — It states the rule too absolutely and removes exceptions, limits or conditions found in the Study Text.

Exam cue: Fit-and-proper is a three-part standard: minimum criteria, examination requirements and CPE. Watch for bankruptcy, judgment-debtor status, fraud/dishonesty/violence convictions and doubtful competence/judgment.
reducing overall portfolio risk when assets with low or imperfect correlation are combined.
removing all systematic market risk once enough securities are held.
allowing the portfolio to avoid regular review and rebalancing after initial allocation.
improving returns mainly by concentrating capital in the highest-yielding asset class.

Answer: A — reducing overall portfolio risk when assets with low or imperfect correlation are combined.

Why this is correct:
Diversification works because assets that do not move perfectly together can reduce overall portfolio volatility and improve risk-adjusted return.

Why the other options are wrong:
B — “removing all systematic market risk once enough securities are held” is not the best answer because the question is testing suitability, diversification and asset-allocation principles, and this option changes or misapplies that rule.
C — “allowing the portfolio to avoid regular review and rebalancing after initial allocation” is not the best answer because the question is testing suitability, diversification and asset-allocation principles, and this option changes or misapplies that rule.
D — “improving returns mainly by concentrating capital in the highest-yielding asset class” is not the best answer because the question is testing suitability, diversification and asset-allocation principles, and this option changes or misapplies that rule.

Exam cue: Diversification reduces risk; it does not guarantee profit, remove systematic risk, or remove the need for portfolio review.
As a related assessment point, which statement about PIDM is BEST aligned with the IPPC study text? Assume the client asks the same question after reading the disclosure document.
PIDM protection is only RM50,000 for takaful.
PIDM protects eligible takaful and insurance benefits up to RM500,000.
PIDM has no role in insurance/takaful benefits.

Answer: B — PIDM protects eligible takaful and insurance benefits up to RM500,000.

Why this is correct:
PIDM administers takaful and insurance benefits protection within the relevant limits.

Why the other options are wrong:
A — It overstates or misidentifies what PIDM protects.
C — This overstates protection or removes risks that still remain under the Study Text.
D — It overstates or misidentifies what PIDM protects.

Exam cue: PIDM questions are coverage traps: eligible deposits are protected up to RM250,000 per depositor per member bank; investment products such as unit trusts, bonds, NIDs, repos, investment accounts and structured products are not deposits.
Which statement correctly applies option rights, payoffs, premiums and exercise features?
Premium equals intrinsic value divided by time value.
Option premium consists of intrinsic value plus time value.

Answer: D — Option premium consists of intrinsic value plus time value.

Why this is correct:
Option value comprises intrinsic and time value.

Why the other options are wrong:
A — “Premium excludes time value” is not the best answer because the question is testing option rights, payoffs, premiums and exercise features, and this option changes or misapplies that rule.
B — “Premium equals intrinsic value divided by time value” is not the best answer because the question is testing option rights, payoffs, premiums and exercise features, and this option changes or misapplies that rule.
C — “Premium equals par value” is not the best answer because the question is testing option rights, payoffs, premiums and exercise features, and this option changes or misapplies that rule.

Exam cue: Derivative questions test rights and obligations: forwards are OTC/customised, futures are exchange-traded/standardised, calls give the right to buy, puts give the right to sell and option buyers have limited loss to premium.
Which statement about the applicable guidelines is correct?
Suitability applies only after a customer complaint.
Suitability assessment is irrelevant for retail customers.
Financial institutions should not recommend products unless reasonably satisfied that they are suitable for the customer.
Recommendations may be based only on commission.

Answer: C — Financial institutions should not recommend products unless reasonably satisfied that they are suitable for the customer.

Why this is correct:
Customer suitability procedures require understanding objectives, needs, horizon and risk appetite.

Why the other options are wrong:
A — Suitability must be assessed before recommendation, not only after a complaint.
B — Retail customers need suitability protection, not less protection.
D — Recommendations must be based on suitability and reasonable basis, not commission alone.

Exam cue: Guidelines questions usually test governance controls: Board/Senior Management oversight, fair treatment, new-product risk controls, suitability, disclosure and documented procedures.
